subject.title: Bug: sandbox.mode: "non-main" silently breaks sessions_spawn subagent initialization

question: Should sandboxed subagent startup failures preserve the asynchronous accepted response and then terminalize with a typed/logged child failure, or should `sessions_spawn` preflight enough sandbox startup work to reject before returning accepted?
rationale: That choice affects the public async spawn contract, registry/session state, gateway wait behavior, and the overlapping lifecycle work, so automation should not choose the permanent behavior alone.

options.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
options.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a visible typed/logged terminal startup failure in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

options.title: Preflight Sandbox Before Accept
options.body: Move enough sandbox startup validation before acceptance to fail fast, accepting extra spawn latency and compatibility review.

options.title: Defer To Lifecycle Tracker
options.body: Keep this sandbox-specific issue open while resolving the broader lifecycle contract in https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/58776 and replacing the conflicting PR.

recommendation.title: Terminalize Async Startup Failure
recommendation.body: Keep the accepted response contract and add a visible typed/logged terminal startup failure in session history, subagent list, and agent wait.

likelyOwner.reason: The history ties this person to the sandbox inheritance guard and the gateway/subagent lifecycle contract that the decision affects.
